title: Cyber Heist: Data Run Edition
premise: A neon courier navigates a compact 3D cyber court, steals a floating data core, and slams it into a glowing uplink hoop while evading roaming security drones.
interaction_model: Mobile-first third-person arcade action using a virtual joystick for movement and a single context-sensitive action button for jumping or dunking/jacking in.
objective: Collect the spawned core, carry it to the hoop zone, perform a dunk to score, and survive as long as possible without colliding with drones.
progression: Score increases one point per successful dunk; a new core respawns after each score; additional drone hazards are added every two points, raising survival pressure over time.
theme: Cyberpunk sports-heist mashup with glowing neon courts, data-core fiction, and drone security threats.
mood: Fast, stylish, arcade-like, tense, and energetic with flashy sci-fi feedback.
likely_audience: players who enjoy short score-chasing sessions
confidence_notes: High confidence in the gameplay loop, controls, scoring, and failure conditions because they are directly defined in code.
Moderate confidence in the final thematic naming because the browser title references 'Cyber Hoops: Dunk Drift' while the start screen branding reads 'Cyber Heist: Data Run Edition'.
High confidence that the intended platform priority is touch/mobile due to the virtual joystick, touch event handlers, safe-area layout, and large action button.
recreation_prompt: Create a mobile-first 3D arcade action game set on a neon cyber court where the player controls a glowing courier from a third-person elevated camera view. The player uses a virtual joystick on the lower left to move and a single large action button on the lower right that normally makes the character jump, but changes into a dunk or jack-in command when the player is carrying the objective and is close enough to the hoop. At the start of each run, place the character near one end of the arena, spawn a floating glowing data core somewhere ahead on the floor, and place a few roaming drone hazards that bounce around the court. The core gameplay loop is: move to collect the data core, carry it safely to the glowing hoop or uplink near the far end, trigger a dramatic slam-dunk style score action, then spawn another core and continue. Each successful dunk adds 1 point and periodically increases difficulty by spawning more drones, turning the game into a score-chasing survival challenge. A collision with a drone should immediately end the run and show a game-over overlay with final score and retry options. Present the game with strong cyberpunk styling: dark background, cyan and orange neon accents, glowing court markings, a holographic backboard, animated pulsing effects, juicy particle bursts on scoring, and clear HUD messaging such as whether the player should secure the core or reach the uplink. Include start, pause, and game-over screens, quick arcade audio cues, success and failure reaction cards, and a smooth camera that follows the player during gameplay while the start screen uses a showcase orbit.
